transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Eve (CTO - Argentum), Marcus (Head of Security), Sophie (Infra), Tom H. (Legal Ops)

Optional auto sections (brief):
Topics: SOC2 evidence, ISO readiness, SSO/SAML onboarding, RBAC model, audit logs & retention, KMS options, Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

--- Summary (auto) ---
Redwood and Argentum run through security controls and deployment options. Argentum is sensitive to custody of keys, long-term retention policies for logs, and proof of SOC2/ISO. They prefer private deployment for regulated workloads but want cost and latency tradeoffs evaluated. Action items captured for both sides.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Eve: Hey hi, it's Eve here — CTO for Argentum — Marcus is on as well.
[00:07] Marcus: Marcus, yep.
[00:08] Sophie: Sophie, infra.
[00:09] Tom: Tom H., legal ops.
[00:11] Maya: Great, I have Jon from our infra/SE side. Jon say hi.
[00:14] Jon: Hey all, hi. I'll be the technical deep dive person.
[00:17] Maya: High level agenda — quick background, security posture questions, then dig into deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), KMS, SSO, audit logs, and finish with next steps. Fine?
[00:23] Eve: Yep, sounds good.

[00:30] Marcus: Just to set expectations — Argentum is a regulated asset manager, we need audit evidence, we have a procurement requirement for SOC2 Type II and we also evaluate ISO27001. Our questions: can Redwood provide those artifacts? what about SSO/SAML integration with our Okta? and how do you handle KMS?

[00:50] Maya: Great — short answers up front: we can share SOC2 Type II report (redacted), our ISO summary, and our SSO docs. For keys we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) across Dedicated and Private. For Hosted there are additional contractual controls for BYOK, and we can talk through network isolation for Private.

[01:15] Sophie: For the BYOK: do you let us bring a Cloud KMS key and have it used for model storage/encryption at rest, or is it only for specific buckets?

[01:23] Jon: Good question. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can plug in your KMS — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HashiCorp Vault. Keys can be used for disk encryption and S3 object encryption (or equivalent). On Hosted we have a BYOK flow but it depends on contract — typically envelope encryption where we hold service keys encrypted by your KMS.

[01:42] Marcus: That envelope model — do we ever see plaintext keys or have Redwood personnel access?

[01:47] Jon: No, we don't have access to your plaintext keys. Our control plane has RBAC and audit logs; key usage events are logged. There's a distinction: in Private/on-prem you control the HSM/KMS fully; in Hosted we manage the runtime but can integrate with your KMS to wrap service keys.

[02:05] Tom: From a legal POV we need to understand data flows for PII-ish telemetry. Are transcripts or chat logs stored, and if so, what's the retention model?

[02:13] Maya: We do retain logs, but retention is configurable per-customer and per-deployment. Out of the box our Hosted offering retains 90 days for detailed logs but you can request longer retention as a paid option; for Dedicated and Private you control retention policy in your environment.

[02:30] Eve: And encryption at rest for Hosted — is it AES-256? is that covered by your SOC2?

[02:36] Jon: Yes, AES-256 or the cloud provider's default strong encryption — documented in our security pack. SOC2 covers our control environment for Hosted; we can provide the Type II report redacted.

[02:48] Marcus: How about SSO: we use Okta with SAML and SCIM provisioning. Can Redwood integrate for admin SSO and API key provisioning?

[02:57] Maya: Yes we support SAML SSO for console access and SCIM for provisioning. API keys lifecycle can be controlled via RBAC — we can map Okta groups to Redwood roles.

[03:08] Sophie: Is there support for step-up MFA for sensitive actions like key rotation or exporting logs?

[03:14] Jon: We support enforcement of MFA via SAML IdP for console; step-up for specific API actions can be enforced through RBAC and approval workflows if integrated via Private deployments and your auth flows. Hosted has role-based controls and audit trails.

[03:30] Eve: Can you describe the RBAC model briefly?

[03:33] Jon: Sure — we have built-in roles (admin, developer, read-only, billing) and custom role definitions where you can allow/deny actions at resource granularity (models, endpoints, billing). For Dedicated/Private you can sync groups from SCIM; for Hosted you can do group mapping via SAML + SCIM.

[03:50] Marcus: Do audit logs include request/response payloads or just metadata? For forensics we need at least request metadata and identifiers; storing full user prompts may be considered PII.

[03:59] Jon: By default we log metadata (request id, user, model, tokens, latency) and we store request/response content only if you enable persisted logs for debug/troubleshooting. That persistence is opt-in and can be encrypted with your KMS.

[04:20] Tom: If we enable persisted logs for debugging, can we restrict access to a small set of engineers and tie it to SSO groups?

[04:27] Maya: Yes, that's standard. RBAC + audit trail will show who accessed what and when.

[04:31] Eve: There's also regulatory requirement for log retention for 7 years in some of our markets — is that realistic with Redwood Hosted?

[04:38] Jon: 7 years is long, but doable — for Hosted we'd need to discuss storage costs and retention SLA; Dedicated/Private gives you direct control. We often advise common pattern: keep metadata long-term and purge sensitive payloads sooner, or offload logs to your S3/GCS with lifecycle policies.

[04:59] Marcus: On compliance evidence: will you provide your vendor SOC2 report to our security team or only via an NDA?

[05:05] Maya: We'll share the redacted SOC2 Type II under an NDA until contract is finalized. ISO summary we can share as well. I'll include both in the packet.

[05:13] Marcus: Perfect.

[05:20] Eve: Now about network isolation — for Dedicated do you provide VPC peering, private endpoints? Sophie can speak to our VPC design.

[05:28] Sophie: Yes, we require private endpoints and egress control. We also have strict subnets for regulated services.

[05:33] Jon: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private you can run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem; we have an option where the data plane is inside your network and control plane is managed through a private control channel.

[05:47] Sophie: Does that private control channel open outbound only?

[05:50] Jon: Typically yes — outbound-only TLS to our control plane endpoints with mutual TLS optional for Private. For fully air-gapped deployments we offer an on-prem bundle — it's more involved but possible.

[06:03] Marcus: How do you handle incident response and notifications? Do we get SOC-type alerts or a dedicated incident channel?

[06:10] Maya: We have an incident management process and we can integrate with customer SLAs for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers get status page and can opt into email/SMS incident alerts; enterprise customers get a PagerDuty/Slack integration and a named CSM for escalations.

[06:23] Tom: We also need contractual guarantees around data residency — can we pin data to a region?

[06:29] Jon: Yes, region pinning is supported across Hosted (in supported regions), Dedicated, and Private. We'll include a region list in the docs.

[06:36] Eve: Performance note — we need latency <100ms p99 for small chat payloads. Is that achievable on Hosted or do we need Dedicated?

[06:45] Jon: For p99 <100ms it's very workload dependent. Hosted in a nearby region can sometimes hit low 100's; Dedicated pooled GPUs with colocated infra will give more consistent p99. We'll do a latency/cost estimate in the follow-up.

[07:00] Sophie: Also curious about model variants and fallback. If you do autoscaling, do you ever route to a different model that might change output distribution?

[07:08] Maya: We have routing policies — by default we route to the pinned model version; if capacity is constrained we can route to a compatible variant and flag that in the response. That behavior is configurable per-route.

[07:19] Marcus: Any encryption in transit specifics beyond TLS? HSTS, mutual TLS?

[07:23] Jon: We use TLS1.2+/TLS1.3 for transport. For Private we can configure mTLS for the control channel. HSTS is supported on web endpoints.

[07:33] Eve: On the SOC2 side — do you have penetration testing reports or third-party assessment summaries?

[07:39] Maya: We have penetration test summaries and high-level remediation notes we can share under NDA. Full reports are usually restricted but we'll provide the summary and attestations.

[07:49] Tom: For contract negotiations we'll need to append security addendums covering breach notifications, data handling, and subprocessor lists.

[07:56] Maya: Yep — we'll provide our standard security addendum and subprocessor list.

[08:01] Marcus: A technical question — KV cache, can that be disabled for regulatory workloads if we don't want any caching persisted?

[08:09] Jon: Yes, caching can be disabled per-deployment or per-route. For regulated workloads you can turn off prefix/KV caching. Note that this will affect latency/cost.

[08:21] Sophie: What's the default retention window on audit logs on Hosted now?

[08:25] Maya: Default is 90 days for detailed logs, 365 days for aggregated metrics. But configurable.

[08:31] Eve: For the pilot we'd like to try Hosted for speed to market but with strict controls — can we request a dedicated tenant with VPC peering and BYOK?

[08:40] Jon: We can provision a dedicated tenant which sits in our Dedicated offering model — effectively reserved capacity with network isolation and BYOK. That might be the middle ground.

[08:50] Marcus: What about RBAC auditability — can we export the audit logs to our SIEM (Splunk) in near real-time?

[08:57] Jon: Yes, we have a streaming API to push audit events to your SIEM via Kinesis or Pub/Sub or a webhook; delivery guarantees vary but near real-time is supported.

[09:10] Tom: Are there any legal restrictions on having data forwarded to third-party telemetry vendors?

[09:15] Maya: We'll list subprocessors and you can request removal or controls for specific vendors; contractual terms are typical.

[09:21] Eve: Okay let's talk about timeline: we're targeting a pilot with production guardrails by Jan 2026. Is that feasible?

[09:29] Jon: Yes, Jan is reasonable. Pilot scope will determine the effort: Hosted dedicated tenant + BYOK + SCIM SSO is usually a few weeks; Dedicated pools with network peering and custom KMS may take longer for procurement.

[09:41] Marcus: One more: retention and eDiscovery — if legal asks for data older than retention, can Redwood do ad-hoc retrieval?

[09:48] Jon: If data is purged per retention policy, it's unrecoverable. We advise keeping an archival copy off-platform if retention windows are short. We can support export hooks to push to your archive before purging.

[09:59] Sophie: What's the model for key rotation? Can we rotate keys without downtime?

[10:05] Jon: We support key rotation with minimal impact using envelope encryption; rotation is seamless for most operations but you'll see a small window where cached tokens may need refresh. For Private you control rotation fully.

[10:20] Maya: We're about halfway through our time — any burning concerns we haven't covered?

[10:24] Marcus: How granular are logs for admin actions — do we log who rotated a key, who changed RBAC?

[10:29] Jon: Yes, admin actions are audited with user id, timestamp, action, and resource. Those logs can be exported.

[10:36] Eve: For the pilot, we'd like to scope two flows — non-regulated user-facing chat on Hosted and a regulated workflow on Dedicated. Can you outline the delta in controls?

[10:46] Maya: Sure — Hosted: faster onboarding, managed runtime, standard controls, shared tenancy with tenant isolation, BYOK options limited; Dedicated: reserved capacity in a customer-dedicated pool, stronger network isolation, BYOK and VPC peering, dedicated support and SLAs; Private: bring entire stack into your VPC/on-prem with maximum control. We'll send a matrix.

[11:10] Jon: Also note that Dedicated supports custom kernel/quantization profiles and predictable latency which helps for low p99 targets.

[11:20] Marcus: Onboarding requirements for us: NDA, redacted SOC2, SCIM + SAML config, KMS endpoints, and a runbook for incident response.

[11:28] Maya: We'll schedule a follow-up to collect those items.

[11:32] Tom: Contract question — we might need breach notification within 72 hours and assistance with forensics. Is that acceptable?

[11:39] Maya: That aligns with our enterprise terms — we'll share our standard security addendum and we can negotiate.

[11:45] Eve: Anything else on your side Jon?

[11:48] Jon: Nothing new — I'll prepare the pilot architecture doc and the latency/cost estimate.

[11:53] Maya: I'll send the compliance pack (SOC2 Type II redacted, ISO summary, penetration test summary), our standard security addendum, subprocessor list, and SCIM/SAML integration guide.

[12:00] Marcus: Great. Quick nit: when you share SOC2, include the effective date and scope so we can map controls.

[12:06] Maya: Will do.

[12:10] Sophie: We'll gather our VPC diagrams and KMS provider details and share with Jon.

[12:15] Tom: Legal will review the security addendum once it's delivered.

[12:19] Maya: Awesome. Before we close, recap of next steps?

[12:24] Eve: Go ahead Maya.

[12:26] Maya: Redwood will: (1) share SOC2 Type II redacted, ISO summary, pen-test summary, security addendum and subprocessor list (by 2025-11-01); (2) Jon will share pilot architecture and latency/cost estimate (by 2025-11-05); (3) Sophie/Argentum to share VPC diagram + KMS details (by 2025-11-03); (4) schedule pilot planning session — we'll propose times next week.

[12:48] Marcus: Sounds good.

[12:50] Eve: Thanks — this was useful.

[12:53] Maya: Thank you all, we'll send notes and the packet.

[12:56] Jon: Thanks everyone.

[13:00] Call ends.

--- End transcript ---

References/attachments mentioned: "SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf (to be shared)", "ISO27001_summary.pdf", "SCIM_SAML_guide.md", "Pilot_Architecture_Template.xlsx"

Recap (short): Redwood demonstrated controls and options for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Main customer concerns captured and mapped to action items. Agreed timeline for pilot planning and document exchange.
